sentences.en: Ava and Maria are joined in the woman my voice celebrates.
sentences.zh: 伊娃和玛丽亚，在我声音所赞颂的那位女性身上合二为一。

sentences.en: For more than names, they are one name, as two eyes make up a single gaze, and more than hands, the hand held out in time of troubles,
sentences.zh: 她们不仅仅是名字，她们是一个名字，就像双眼构成单一的凝视；她们不仅仅是双手，更是在困境中伸出的援手，

sentences.en: and more than eyes, the eyes of she who gives faith with her look, so that the lonely man may raise his face towards her feet,
sentences.zh: 她们不仅仅是双眼，更是那位用目光给予信仰之人的双眼，让孤独的人能抬起脸庞望向她的双足，

sentences.en: and see in the moon and the stars above the earth of our fatherland.
sentences.zh: 并从我们祖国大地之上的月亮与星辰中看到这一切。

sentences.en: Ava and Maria, Maria, Ava transfigured into hope.
sentences.zh: 伊娃和玛丽亚，玛丽亚，伊娃，化身为希望。

sentences.en: So that was Glory by the Peronist writer,
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是那位庇隆主义作家所写的《荣耀》，

sentences.en: José María Castañeda de Dios, which he wrote in 1951.
sentences.zh: 何塞·玛丽亚·卡斯塔涅达·德·迪奥斯，写于1951年。
zh_words: 何塞·玛丽亚·卡斯塔涅达·德·迪奥斯

sentences.en: And Dominic, that's one of your favourite poems, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，那是你最喜欢的诗之一，对吧？

sentences.en: It's a very strange poem, Tom.
sentences.zh: 那是一首非常奇怪的诗，汤姆。

sentences.en: I think I, as I told you, a bizarre and terrible poem.
sentences.zh: 正如我告诉你的，我认为这是一首离奇而可怕的诗。

sentences.en: And José María Castañeda de Dios was actually quite a serious poet.
sentences.zh: 而何塞·玛丽亚·卡斯塔涅达·德·迪奥斯实际上是一位相当严肃的诗人。
zh_words: 何塞·玛丽亚·卡斯塔涅达·德·迪奥斯

sentences.en: He lived until his 90s.
sentences.zh: 他活到了90多岁。

sentences.en: He was kind of a fated...
sentences.zh: 他算是一个命中注定的……

sentences.en: So what was he thinking?
sentences.zh: 那他当时在想什么？

sentences.en: Argentine writer.
sentences.zh: 阿根廷作家。

sentences.en: Well, he was a member as a young man of this official Ava Peron poet circle, and they would meet at the headquarters of her foundation every week, I think,
sentences.zh: 嗯，他年轻时是这个官方伊娃·庇隆诗人圈子的成员，我想他们每周或每月都会在她的基金会总部聚会，

sentences.en: or every month, and they would read poems about Ava Peron.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会朗诵关于伊娃·庇隆的诗歌。

sentences.en: And the fact that somebody who's actually quite a serious literary figure was writing this unbelievable nonsense.
sentences.zh: 而一个实际上相当严肃的文学人物竟然在写这种令人难以置信的胡言乱语，这事实本身……

sentences.en: Dros.
sentences.zh: 废话。

sentences.en: Yeah, dros is the word.
sentences.zh: 没错，就是废话。

sentences.en: It reminds me a bit of the ode to Nicola Sturgeon that schoolchildren did on TV a few months into the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 这让我想起几个月前疫情期间，小学生在电视上朗诵的那首赞美尼古拉·斯特金的颂歌。

sentences.en: Very similar figures.
sentences.zh: 非常相似的人物。

sentences.en: Where they kind of hailed her.
sentences.zh: 他们在那儿吹捧她。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, yeah, a certain similarity.
sentences.zh: 嗯，确实，有某种相似之处。

sentences.en: And Maria, presumably, is the virgin in that.
sentences.zh: 而玛丽亚，大概就是指其中的圣母吧。

sentences.en: Well, I think the thing is, Maria was one of her names.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为关键在于，玛丽亚是她的名字之一。

sentences.en: So it's a sort of play on the fact that Maria is one of her names, but also Maria is obviously the virgin.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种文字游戏，既利用了玛丽亚是她名字之一的事实，同时也显然暗指玛丽亚是圣母。

sentences.en: And the stuff about looking towards her, she gives faith with her look.
sentences.zh: 还有关于仰望她的内容，她用目光给予信仰。

sentences.en: You raise your face towards her feet.
sentences.zh: 你抬起脸庞望向她的双足。

sentences.en: She's transfigured into hope.
sentences.zh: 她化身为希望。

sentences.en: I mean, there's obvious Catholic resonances there, aren't there?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这里有明显的宗教共鸣，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Which are there by this point.
sentences.zh: 到了这个阶段，这些共鸣已经存在了。

sentences.en: So this is 1951 that he writes this, as you said.
sentences.zh: 所以正如你所说，这是他在1951年写的。

sentences.en: By that point, the cult of Evita.
sentences.zh: 到了那个时候，对艾薇塔的崇拜……

sentences.en: We never talked about Evita.
sentences.zh: 我们从未谈论过艾薇塔。

sentences.en: Evita kind of means, you know, dear little Ava kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 艾薇塔的意思大概是，你知道，亲爱的小伊娃之类的。

sentences.en: Kind of affectionate.
sentences.zh: 带有一种亲昵感。

sentences.en: Eva Kins.
sentences.zh: 伊娃·金斯。

sentences.en: Eva Kins is a bit, yeah, a bit unlikely, but it's a kind of affectionate diminutive.
sentences.zh: 伊娃·金斯有点，嗯，不太可能，但它是一种亲昵的指小词。

sentences.en: And I think the cult of Evita by this point in 1951 has become very, very firmly established.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为到1951年这个阶段，对艾薇塔的崇拜已经非常、非常稳固地确立了。

sentences.en: So it predated her death.
sentences.zh: 所以它早于她的去世。

sentences.en: In the last episode, we were talking about, thanks to her, the efforts of her foundation, people were saying she's the Lady of Hope, the Bridge of Love, which was her favorite
sentences.zh: 在上集里，我们谈到多亏了她，多亏了她基金会的努力，人们称她为“希望女士”、“爱之桥”，这显然是她最喜欢的

sentences.en: nickname, apparently.
sentences.zh: 绰号。

sentences.en: I mean, that stuff is very Marian, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那些东西非常有圣母玛利亚的色彩，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But also, presumably, she's the mother of the nation.
sentences.zh: 但大概她也是国母。

sentences.en: She is bestowing care and attention on the people who are like her children.
sentences.zh: 她正在向那些如同她孩子般的人民倾注关怀与关注。

sentences.en: And this, presumably, is why the ovarian cancer with which she's diagnosed, I mean, must be a psychic wound, as well as being a kind of terrible medical shock.
sentences.zh: 而这大概就是为什么她被诊断出的卵巢癌，我的意思是，除了是一种可怕的医疗打击外，一定也是一种心理创伤。

sentences.en: I mean, this is the story of today's podcast, ultimately, the death of Eva Barron.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这归根结底是今天播客的故事，伊娃·庇隆的去世。

sentences.en: And the fact is that her death becomes much more than a personal event.
sentences.zh: 事实上，她的去世不仅仅是一个个人事件。

sentences.en: It's a kind of political and national one.
sentences.zh: 这是一种政治和国家层面的事件。

sentences.en: So to go back to where we were at the end of the last episode, that cliffhanger, she had gone to the Abayeneda neighborhood to open a taxi driver's union office.
sentences.zh: 回到上一集结尾我们提到的那个悬念，她去了阿韦利亚内达社区为出租车司机工会办公室揭幕。

sentences.en: And she collapsed or fainted, ended up going to a hospital, and basically vanished from the newspapers for four days.
sentences.zh: 然后她晕倒了，进了医院，基本上从报纸上消失了四天。

sentences.en: So this is the beginning of 1950.
sentences.zh: 所以这是1950年初。

sentences.en: And that was very unusual, because this is a point when she's in the newspapers every single day.
sentences.zh: 这非常不寻常，因为当时她每天都会出现在报纸上。

sentences.en: And then after four days, they said, oh, she's actually had appendicitis.
sentences.zh: 四天后，他们说，哦，她其实是得了阑尾炎。

sentences.en: We've taken her appendix out.
sentences.zh: 我们已经切除了她的阑尾。

sentences.en: There's all the procession of churchmen and ministers going to her bedside.
sentences.zh: 接着是一连串的教会人士和部长前往她的床边探视。

sentences.en: But actually, she's probably suffering from the cancer that will kill her, even at this point.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，即使在那个时候，她可能就已经患上了最终夺去她生命的癌症。

sentences.en: And later on, one of the doctors who had looked at her, who was actually the minister of education in the government, a guy called Oskar Ivanisevich.
sentences.zh: 后来，其中一位为她诊治的医生，也就是当时政府的教育部长，一个叫奥斯卡·伊瓦尼塞维奇的人说……

sentences.en: We love to see some multitasking.
sentences.zh: 我们喜欢看到这种多任务处理。

sentences.en: Multitasking, exactly.
sentences.zh: 多任务处理，没错。

sentences.en: Very impressive.
sentences.zh: 非常令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: He said, actually, I looked at her in hospital, and she was suffering from cancer of the uterus.
sentences.zh: 他说，实际上，我在医院检查过她，她患的是子宫癌。

sentences.en: And we did tests.
sentences.zh: 我们做了检查。

sentences.en: And I suggested to her, you should have a hysterectomy.
sentences.zh: 我建议她应该做子宫切除术。

sentences.en: And she loses it, doesn't she?
sentences.zh: 然后她崩溃了，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, she's really, really upset by this idea.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她对这个想法感到非常、非常不安。

sentences.en: The trouble is with this.
sentences.zh: 问题就在这里。

sentences.en: Now we're getting into territory from this point onwards that is quite murky, because everybody has very vested interests.
sentences.zh: 现在我们进入了一个从这一点开始相当模糊的领域，因为每个人都有非常既定的利益。

sentences.en: They're all telling slightly different stories.
sentences.zh: 他们都在讲述略有不同的故事。

sentences.en: But I think it's perfectly possible that he said to her, perhaps not in so many words, he said, there is something seriously wrong with you, and we would like to do an operation.
sentences.zh: 但我认为完全有可能他曾对她说，也许没有用那么多字眼，他说，你的身体出了严重的问题，我们想做一个手术。

sentences.en: And she said, no, no way.
sentences.zh: 而她说，不，绝不可能。

sentences.en: Absolutely not.
sentences.zh: 绝对不行。

sentences.en: Under no circumstances.
sentences.zh: 无论如何都不行。

sentences.en: I think there might be a slight element of, perhaps, a paranoia.
sentences.zh: 我认为这可能带有一点点偏执的成分。

sentences.en: But also, some of her biographers say, at that point, she sees herself as the mother of the nation, and all that kind of thing, as you were saying, Tom.
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，汤姆，她的一些传记作者说，在那个时候，她把自己视为国母，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And the idea of such an operation is anathema to her.
sentences.zh: 而进行这样的手术对她来说是不可接受的。

sentences.en: What's odd about it is that not only had Perron's first wife had it, but her mother, Ava's mother had had it, and had been operated on, and it had been fine.
sentences.zh: 奇怪的是，不仅庇隆的第一任妻子做过这个手术，连她的母亲，伊娃的母亲也做过，而且手术很成功。

sentences.en: She was still alive.
sentences.zh: 她还活着。

sentences.en: So it's not like it's a total mystery to her.
sentences.zh: 所以这并不是什么完全未知的谜团。

sentences.en: And isn't she, when she goes on her tours, she's taking kind of cotton wool with her to deal with the hemorrhaging that she's starting to experience.
sentences.zh: 而且当她去巡视时，她不是带着棉花来处理她开始经历的出血吗？

sentences.en: So, I mean, she must have a sense of both how serious it is, but also an awareness that catching it early is the best thing to do.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，她一定既意识到情况有多严重，也意识到尽早治疗是最好的做法。

sentences.en: But she wouldn't be the first person in history, or indeed the last, to have something seriously wrong with them and just deny it to themselves.
sentences.zh: 但她绝不是历史上第一个，也不会是最后一个身体出了严重问题却选择自我否认的人。

sentences.en: I'll carry on.
sentences.zh: 我会继续坚持。

sentences.en: Maybe it'll go away.
sentences.zh: 也许它会自己消失。

sentences.en: Is cancer a cause of embarrassment at that period?
sentences.zh: 在那个时期，癌症是一个令人尴尬的原因吗？

sentences.en: I mean, is it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，是吗？

sentences.en: You don't talk about it.
sentences.zh: 你不会谈论它。

sentences.en: I think you don't talk about it.
sentences.zh: 我想你不会谈论它。

sentences.en: I think there's a combination of not talking about cancer generally, a fear, obviously, that it's a death sentence, and so you don't talk about it.
sentences.zh: 我认为这结合了普遍不谈论癌症的习惯，显然还有对它作为死亡判决的恐惧，所以你不会谈论它。

sentences.en: Because at this point in history, people are aware of it in a way they'd not been aware of it centuries previously.
sentences.zh: 因为在历史的这个阶段，人们对它的认知与几个世纪前不同。

sentences.en: You're not yet at a point where people are saying, listen, we can fix this.
sentences.zh: 你还没有达到人们会说“听着，我们可以治好这个”的阶段。

sentences.en: Even though there's an argument that they could have fixed this.
sentences.zh: 尽管有一种观点认为他们本可以治好它。

sentences.en: But I think also that particular kind of, you know, anything gynecological is simply not discussed in a very Catholic country like Argentina.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，在阿根廷这样一个非常天主教的国家，任何妇科方面的问题根本就不会被讨论。

sentences.en: These things aren't really aired publicly.
sentences.zh: 这些事情并没有真正公开地被谈论。

sentences.en: And what about Perron, whose first wife had had this?
sentences.zh: 那庇隆呢，他的第一任妻子也得过这个病？

sentences.en: What's going on there?
sentences.zh: 那里发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, here's the interesting thing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有趣的地方就在这里。

sentences.en: His biographers, I mean, Joseph Page, one of his biographers, says of Perron, Perron always had a very peculiar attitude towards doctors and medicine.
sentences.zh: 他的传记作者，我的意思是，约瑟夫·佩奇，他的传记作者之一，谈到庇隆时说，庇隆对医生和医学的态度一直非常古怪。

sentences.en: He often said doctors are useless.
sentences.zh: 他经常说医生是没用的。

sentences.en: He came from a family where there were doctors in the family, and there'd been talk of him becoming a doctor.
sentences.zh: 他来自一个有医生的家庭，而且曾有人谈论过让他成为一名医生。

sentences.en: And there are suggestions that he rather fancied himself as a kind of amateur doctor.
sentences.zh: 有迹象表明他相当自诩为一名业余医生。

sentences.en: And it is possible that he would have said to her, don't worry about it.
sentences.zh: 他很有可能曾对她说，别担心。

sentences.en: It'll be fine.
sentences.zh: 会没事的。

sentences.en: Doctors are a load of quacks anyway, because he did say such things.
sentences.zh: 反正医生都是一群庸医，因为他确实说过这样的话。

sentences.en: So we don't know.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不知道。

sentences.en: We have no evidence for it, but it is possible.
sentences.zh: 我们没有证据，但这是有可能的。

sentences.en: All that we know is when she's recovered from this turn at the beginning of 1950, she throws herself back into her work in an incredibly manic way.
sentences.zh: 我们只知道，当她在1950年初从这次病情中恢复过来后，她以一种极其狂躁的方式重新投入到工作中。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because she says, doesn't she, I don't have time for medical treatment.
sentences.zh: 因为她说，不是吗，我没有时间接受医疗。

sentences.en: Treatments are for oligarchs.
sentences.zh: 治疗是给寡头准备的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Which is a very, you know, she's dramatizing it in a very political way.
sentences.zh: 这非常，你知道，她以一种非常政治化的方式将其戏剧化了。

sentences.en: But also, Tom, her whole life she's lived as a soap opera.
sentences.zh: 但汤姆，她的一生都像是一部肥皂剧。

sentences.en: I mean, that's soap operas that she made her name in.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那是她成名的肥皂剧。

sentences.en: And her politics and her public life she has conducted as a melodramatic soap opera.
sentences.zh: 而她的政治和公共生活，她也是以一种情节剧式的肥皂剧方式进行的。

sentences.en: And the idea of sacrifice has been there from the beginning in her adult persona.
sentences.zh: 牺牲的概念从她成年人格的最初就一直存在。

sentences.en: Oh, so you think it might be kind of willed that she's offering herself up as a blood sacrifice or to Argentina?
sentences.zh: 哦，所以你认为她可能是有意为之，她把自己作为一种血祭献给阿根廷？

sentences.en: It's really hard to say.
sentences.zh: 这真的很难说。

sentences.en: People do have martyr complexes.
sentences.zh: 人们确实有殉道情结。

sentences.en: We've talked about some very peculiar characters and the rest is history.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论过一些非常古怪的人物，剩下的就是历史了。

sentences.en: You know, we've already made the comparison with Catherine of Siena, people who seem to have a kind of a will to sacrifice themselves.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们已经做过与锡耶纳的凯瑟琳的比较，有些人似乎有一种牺牲自己的意愿。

sentences.en: Her biographers, Fraser and Navarro, say at one point, of all the distortion, that surround David Peron's life, the least outrageous and the closest to the truth is
sentences.zh: 她的传记作者弗雷泽和纳瓦罗在某个地方说，在围绕大卫·庇隆生活的所有扭曲中，最不离谱且最接近真相的是

sentences.en: the suggestion that she elected to die for Peron, Peronism.
sentences.zh: 她选择为庇隆、为庇隆主义而死的说法。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I mean, that is a bizarre thing to say of somebody.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对某人说出这样的话真是离奇。

sentences.en: Even Peron himself, you know, said she worked herself to the bone.
sentences.zh: 即使是庇隆本人，你知道，也说她工作得太拼命了。

sentences.en: I begged her to slow down.
sentences.zh: 我恳求她慢下来。

sentences.en: She wouldn't.
sentences.zh: 她不肯。

sentences.en: It's this sense she has that she can't afford to lie around in hospital because that's oligarchical.
sentences.zh: 这是一种她觉得无法躺在医院里的感觉，因为那是寡头行为。

sentences.en: Is it also compounded by the fact that things are starting to go not quite as well for Peron by this point?
sentences.zh: 这是否也因为庇隆在这一点上情况开始不太顺利而加剧了？

sentences.en: I think so.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: I think there's a sense of pressure generally within the regime.
sentences.zh: 我认为整个政权内部有一种普遍的压力感。

sentences.en: We talked in the previous episodes about how Peron took over at a sort of ideal Goldilocks moment for Argentina.
sentences.zh: 我们在之前的剧集中谈到庇隆是如何在阿根廷一个理想的“金发姑娘时刻”接管政权的。

sentences.en: The Second World War has happened.
sentences.zh: 第二次世界大战已经发生。

sentences.en: There's a great demand for Argentine exports in Europe, but there's not imports coming the other way.
sentences.zh: 欧洲对阿根廷出口产品的需求很大，但却没有进口产品进来。

sentences.en: But actually what's happening by the, when you get into the 1950s is prices are starting to go up.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，当你进入1950年代时，价格开始上涨。

sentences.en: The returns they get in for exports are starting to go down.
sentences.zh: 他们从出口中获得的回报开始下降。

sentences.en: The unions are restive.
sentences.zh: 工会开始不安。

sentences.en: There's a railway strike, which for the first time means the government is against the unions.

sentences.en: Because people from this point onwards, December 1951, they start to have masses for her.
sentences.zh: 因为从那时起，也就是1951年12月，人们开始为她举行弥撒。

sentences.en: They have candlelit vigils and all this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 他们举行烛光守夜活动，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And is there a kind of maybe a Shakespearean quality in the sense that in Shakespeare, the king's body is often seen as a metaphor for the state of the nation?
sentences.zh: 这是否有一种莎士比亚式的特质？因为在莎士比亚的作品中，国王的身体常被视为国家状态的隐喻？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think so.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想是这样。

sentences.en: And that her sickness is expressive of a sickness in the government and in Argentina more generally, do you think?
sentences.zh: 你认为她的疾病是否也表达了政府乃至整个阿根廷的某种病态？

sentences.en: And that that's part of what's tied up with it?
sentences.zh: 这是否也是其中纠葛的一部分？

sentences.en: I do think so, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我确实这么认为，汤姆。

sentences.en: I think it's not just a king's body.
sentences.zh: 我认为这不仅仅是国王的身体。

sentences.en: It's also kind of the idea of a woman's body as a kind of place onto which often men project fantasies, desires, all those kind of things.
sentences.zh: 这还涉及一种观念，即女性的身体往往是男性投射幻想、欲望以及所有这类事物的地方。

sentences.en: I mean, you don't have to be a sort of super feminist critic, you know, to see the resonance of that, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你不需要成为那种超级女权主义评论家，也能看出其中的共鸣，我想。

sentences.en: People do, for example, there's a place called Luján outside Buenos Aires where there's this sort of mock Gothic basilica where there's a virgin of Luján, of course,
sentences.zh: 人们确实会这样做，例如，布宜诺斯艾利斯郊外有一个叫卢汉的地方，那里有一座仿哥特式的巴西利卡大教堂，当然，那里供奉着卢汉圣母，

sentences.en: who appeared to somebody and did miracles.
sentences.zh: 她曾向某人显灵并创造了奇迹。

sentences.en: And it's the most popular pilgrimage site in Argentina.
sentences.zh: 那是阿根廷最受欢迎的朝圣地。

sentences.en: I mean, I find this so unsettling.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我觉得这太令人不安了。

sentences.en: People who are themselves very sick will make pilgrimages to Luján for Evita.
sentences.zh: 那些本身病得很重的人会为了艾薇塔去卢汉朝圣。

sentences.en: So the classic thing is people with broken legs will supposedly walk there.
sentences.zh: 最典型的例子就是，腿部骨折的人据说会走着去那里。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: And they'll perform a feat.
sentences.zh: 他们会完成一项壮举。

sentences.en: They'll do a sacrifice because they think this will get sort of credit from the Virgin Mary.
sentences.zh: 他们会进行某种牺牲，因为他们认为这能从圣母玛利亚那里获得某种功德。

sentences.en: And they will have kind of inscriptions.
sentences.zh: 他们还会带着某种铭文。

sentences.en: They will carry huge Virgin Mary sort of statues with the inscription,
sentences.zh: 他们会抬着巨大的圣母玛利亚雕像，上面写着，

sentences.en: Por la salud de Evita, for the health of Evita.
sentences.zh: “为了艾薇塔的健康”（Por la salud de Evita）。

sentences.en: And people will start putting it, who don't travel, will put up altars in the street with candles, with the effigies of the Virgin, again, for Evita.
sentences.zh: 那些没去旅行的人也会开始在街上摆放祭坛，点上蜡烛，放上圣母像，同样是为了艾薇塔。

sentences.en: So this is, you know, within weeks of her saying she wouldn't take the vice presidential nomination.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这发生在她宣布不接受副总统提名后的几周内。

sentences.en: And there's a sense that almost she's not going to do it politically, but actually people are pouring that emotional energy into this sort of, you know, overtly religious campaign
sentences.zh: 人们有一种感觉，她似乎不会在政治上采取行动，但实际上，人们正将那种情感能量倾注到这种公开的宗教运动中，

sentences.en: to try and save her life.
sentences.zh: 试图挽救她的生命。

sentences.en: So it is all very...
sentences.zh: 所以这一切非常……

sentences.en: Intense.
sentences.zh: 强烈。

sentences.en: It's very intense.
sentences.zh: 非常强烈。

sentences.en: It is very intense.
sentences.zh: 确实非常强烈。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's incredibly intense.
sentences.zh: 极其强烈。

sentences.en: She has her last 17th of October loyalty rally, which is the anniversary of the day that they'd had that first big thing with Peron when his bosses are trying to kick him out.
sentences.zh: 她举行了最后一次10月17日的忠诚集会，那是他们与庇隆举行第一次大型活动周年纪念日，当时庇隆的反对者正试图把他赶下台。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In which she hadn't actually played a major part, but by now everyone assumes that she has.
sentences.zh: 在那次活动中，她其实并没有发挥主要作用，但现在每个人都认为她发挥了作用。

sentences.en: And now a million and a half people in the center of Argentina.
sentences.zh: 现在阿根廷市中心聚集了一百五十万人。

sentences.en: They've dosed her up on morphine.
sentences.zh: 他们给她注射了大量吗啡。

sentences.en: She is there.
sentences.zh: 她就在那里。

sentences.en: She's now shrunk so much.
sentences.zh: 她现在已经瘦得不成样子了。

sentences.en: She's in this suit that's kind of hanging off her.
sentences.zh: 她穿着那套挂在身上的套装。

sentences.en: Peron makes a tribute to her.
sentences.zh: 庇隆向她致敬。

sentences.en: From this point on, most people are basically talking to her about her as though she's already dead.
sentences.zh: 从这一点开始，大多数人谈论她时，基本上都好像她已经死了一样。

sentences.en: So Peron is giving basically her obituary while she's standing there.
sentences.zh: 所以庇隆在发表悼词时，她就站在那里。

sentences.en: She's standing there.
sentences.zh: 她站在那里。

sentences.en: And she starts crying.
sentences.zh: 她开始哭泣。

sentences.en: She falls into his arMs.
sentences.zh: 她倒在他的怀里。

sentences.en: Again, you can see this in the museum.
sentences.zh: 同样，你可以在博物馆里看到这一幕。

sentences.en: It's treated as though this incredibly sort of solemn moment, which in many ways it is, but it's also ghastly.
sentences.zh: 这被视为一个极其庄严的时刻，在许多方面确实如此，但同时也令人毛骨悚然。

sentences.en: To me, it seems excruciating in the amount of dramatic to be playing this out in public.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，在公共场合上演这种戏剧性场面简直令人痛苦。

sentences.en: But I think she wanted it to be in public.
sentences.zh: 但我认为她希望这一切在公共场合进行。

sentences.en: There's a sense in which her story, in which her public story, in which she has invested so much, must now proceed towards its preordained conclusion.
sentences.zh: 在某种意义上，她投入了如此多心血的公共故事，现在必须走向其预定的结局。

sentences.en: And it must be witnessed by her people.
sentences.zh: 而且必须由她的人民见证。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Now, the thing is, to the people who had never liked her, we talked before about the great writer,
sentences.zh: 问题是，对于那些从未喜欢过她的人来说，我们之前谈到了伟大的作家，

sentences.en: Borges.
sentences.zh: 博尔赫斯。

sentences.en: Borges despised the Perons.
sentences.zh: 博尔赫斯鄙视庇隆夫妇。

sentences.en: He despised Evita.
sentences.zh: 他鄙视艾薇塔。

sentences.en: And for somebody like him, anglophile.
sentences.zh: 对于像他这样亲英的人来说。

sentences.en: Understatement.
sentences.zh: 轻描淡写。

sentences.en: Tweed.
sentences.zh: 粗花呢。

sentences.en: Tweed.
sentences.zh: 粗花呢。

sentences.en: I was about to say,
sentences.zh: 我正想说，

sentences.en: Tweed.
sentences.zh: 粗花呢。

sentences.en: Thinking about Kipling, whatever he's doing.
sentences.zh: 想到吉卜林，无论他在做什么。

sentences.en: Horrendous.
sentences.zh: 太可怕了。

sentences.en: He finds this unbelievably ghastly.
sentences.zh: 他觉得这简直令人作呕。

sentences.en: Just common, embarrassing.
sentences.zh: 简直粗俗，令人尴尬。

sentences.en: Gauche.
sentences.zh: 笨拙。

sentences.en: Morkish.
sentences.zh: 病态。

sentences.en: But I think for most ordinary Argentines, they actually regard it as incredibly moving.
sentences.zh: 但我认为对于大多数普通阿根廷人来说，他们实际上觉得这非常感人。

sentences.en: This woman, they think, has willingly sacrificed her health and her life for her foundation, for her work.
sentences.zh: 他们认为，这个女人为了她的基金会，为了她的工作，心甘情愿地牺牲了自己的健康和生命。

sentences.en: And now she's determined to die in public.
sentences.zh: 现在她决心在公众面前死去。

sentences.en: And they must all, there's almost a sort of, I can't remember whether or not, I used this phrase in a previous episode, but I remember writing it down while I was reading up on it.
sentences.zh: 他们必须……我记不清在之前的节目中是否用过这个短语，但我记得在阅读相关资料时把它记了下来。

sentences.en: There's a kind of totalitarianism of sentimentality about the Peronist regime, I think.
sentences.zh: 我认为庇隆政权有一种“情感极权主义”。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So a sense that you must, you absolutely must subscribe to this high emotional drama, which is Diana, 1997, Tom.
sentences.zh: 所以，你必须，绝对必须认同这种高度的情感戏剧，就像1997年的戴安娜王妃一样，汤姆。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so the conjunction of the film of Evita coming out in 1996 and then Diana dying in 1997 brought that home very forcibly, I think.
sentences.zh: 因此，1996年上映的《艾薇塔》电影与1997年戴安娜王妃去世这两件事结合在一起，我认为非常有力地传达了这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, of course,
sentences.zh: 所以，当然，

sentences.en: Peron wins the election in November.
sentences.zh: 庇隆在11月的选举中获胜。

sentences.en: There is a scene described by an anti-Peronist writer.
sentences.zh: 一位反庇隆主义作家描述了一个场景。

sentences.en: She was in hospital at this point.
sentences.zh: 当时她已经在医院了。

sentences.en: But she votes, doesn't she?
sentences.zh: 但她投票了，不是吗？

sentences.en: And it's the only time that she votes.
sentences.zh: 那是她唯一一次投票。

sentences.en: A special ballot box was made for her and brought to the hospital.
sentences.zh: 一个特制的投票箱被送到医院给她。

sentences.en: She votes in this ballot box.
sentences.zh: 她在那个投票箱里投了票。

sentences.en: They take it outside.
sentences.zh: 他们把它带到外面。

sentences.en: And this radical writer,
sentences.zh: 那位激进派作家，

sentences.en: David Vinyas, said, afterwards, he said, I saw women outside on their knees praying on the sidewalk.
sentences.zh: 大卫·维尼亚斯（David Viñas）后来写道，他说，我看到外面的妇女跪在人行道上祈祷。

sentences.en: And they kept touching the ballot box that held Evita's vote and kissing it.
sentences.zh: 她们不停地触摸装着艾薇塔选票的投票箱并亲吻它。

sentences.en: A fascinating scene worthy of a book by Tolstoy.
sentences.zh: 一个迷人的场景，值得托尔斯泰写进书里。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it is a really weird scene, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个非常奇怪的场景，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, people praying to this ballot box.
sentences.zh: 我是说，人们对着这个投票箱祈祷。

sentences.en: I mean, he's fascinated by the scene, but he's simultaneously made nauseous by the toadying of her admirers.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他被这个场景迷住了，但同时又对她崇拜者的阿谀奉承感到恶心。

sentences.en: So there's a kind of conflict there.
sentences.zh: 所以那里存在一种冲突。

sentences.en: So over the next few months, her health continues to decline, but she doesn't die.
sentences.zh: 接下来的几个月里，她的健康状况持续恶化，但她并没有死。

sentences.en: So actually, the terrible thing for her, or just on a human level, is that this is quite a protracted scene.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，对她来说，或者从人类层面来看，可怕的是这是一个相当漫长的过程。

sentences.en: And actually, by early 1952, she is still being dragged out or dragging herself out to give speeches on the balcony of the Casa Rosada.
sentences.zh: 事实上，到1952年初，她仍然被拖出来，或者自己挣扎着出来，在玫瑰宫的阳台上发表演讲。

sentences.en: But she must be dragging herself out.
sentences.zh: 但她一定是在挣扎着出来。

sentences.en: Because as we've been saying, you know, she, all her suffering has no meaning if it's not public.
sentences.zh: 因为正如我们所说，如果不是公开的，她所有的痛苦都没有意义。

sentences.en: Well, maybe a bit of both.
sentences.zh: 嗯，也许两者都有。

sentences.en: It doesn't hurt the regime to keep dragging her out, by the way, because Argentina is now beginning to get into deeper and deeper kind of economic waters.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，不断把她拖出来对政权并没有坏处，因为阿根廷现在开始陷入越来越深的经济困境。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So it doesn't help for people to be distracted by this great drama.
sentences.zh: 所以人们被这场伟大的戏剧分散注意力并没有什么坏处。

sentences.en: She is now on a lot of drugs and she's in an enormous amount of pain.
sentences.zh: 她现在服用了大量药物，而且承受着巨大的痛苦。

sentences.en: And her speech has become sort of darker and darker now.
sentences.zh: 她的言辞现在变得越来越阴暗了。

sentences.en: So for the first time, really, she is really talking violently.
sentences.zh: 所以这是她第一次真正开始暴力地谈话。

sentences.en: If it is necessary, we will execute justice with our own hands.
sentences.zh: 如果有必要，我们将亲手执行正义。

sentences.en: I will leave nothing standing that is not for Perron.
sentences.zh: 我不会留下任何不属于庇隆的东西。

sentences.en: And then here's an extraordinary one.
sentences.zh: 还有一个非同寻常的例子。

sentences.en: May.
sentences.zh: 五月。

sentences.en: Those who believe in sweetness and love forget that Christ said, I have come to earth to bring fire so that it may burn more.
sentences.zh: 那些相信甜蜜和爱的人忘记了基督说过，我来到世上是为了带来火，让它燃烧得更旺。

sentences.en: He gave us an example of fanaticism.
sentences.zh: 他给了我们一个狂热的榜样。

sentences.en: And for that reason, we must be fanatics for Perron until death.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们必须至死都是庇隆的狂热信徒。

sentences.en: And doesn't she also, from her sickbed, kind of order thousands and thousands of pistols and machine guns and things with the aim of giving in to the trades unions?
sentences.zh: 而且她不是还在病榻上命令工会购买成千上万的手枪和机枪吗？

sentences.en: Oh, I never heard that, Tom.
sentences.zh: 噢，我从未听说过，汤姆。

sentences.en: That is an interesting detail.
sentences.zh: 那是一个有趣的细节。

sentences.en: And behind Perron's back.
sentences.zh: 而且是在庇隆背后。

sentences.en: Behind Perron's back, she's doing this.
sentences.zh: 她在庇隆背后做这件事。

sentences.en: And then after her death,
sentences.zh: 在她死后，

sentences.en: Perron kind of finds out about this and goes and gets them all back.
sentences.zh: 庇隆发现了这件事，并把它们全部收回了。

sentences.en: But she is, I mean, she's not just talking about violence.
sentences.zh: 但她，我的意思是，她不仅仅是在谈论暴力。

sentences.en: She's preparing for violence.
sentences.zh: 她正在为暴力做准备。

sentences.en: If it's, I mean, literally the last thing she does.
sentences.zh: 如果这是……我的意思是，这简直是她做的最后一件事。

sentences.en: So this is an interesting thing.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一件有趣的事情。

sentences.en: There's definitely an apocalyptic tone to her rhetoric in the last year or months of her life.
sentences.zh: 在她生命的最后一年或几个月里，她的言辞中绝对有一种末日般的基调。

sentences.en: And this will be important later on because later on in the 1960s and 1970s, as Argentina slides into terrorism and virtual civil war, people will brandish this.
sentences.zh: 这一点在以后很重要，因为后来在20世纪60年代和70年代，当阿根廷陷入恐怖主义和事实上的内战时，人们会挥舞起这一点。

sentences.en: And they will, this is this Evita that young people will turn to.
sentences.zh: 他们会……这就是年轻人会转向的那个艾薇塔。

sentences.en: The radical, the violent, the terroriSt.
sentences.zh: 那个激进的、暴力的、恐怖主义的艾薇塔。

sentences.en: That's what people will get very excited about.
sentences.zh: 那才是人们会感到非常兴奋的地方。

sentences.en: So let's move forward towards the close of her story.
sentences.zh: 那么让我们继续推进到她故事的结尾。

sentences.en: So we get towards- But just before that,
sentences.zh: 所以我们接近——但在那之前，

sentences.en: I mean, before she dies,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在她去世之前，

sentences.en: I said, you know, about 10 minutes back, that there are very brutal attempts to keep her alive.
sentences.zh: 我大约10分钟前说过，为了让她活下去，人们进行了非常残酷的尝试。

sentences.en: And one of these is radiotherapy.
sentences.zh: 其中之一就是放射治疗。

sentences.en: Oh yeah, terrible.
sentences.zh: 噢，是的，太可怕了。

sentences.en: Which basically just kind of leaves her horribly singed, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 这基本上只是让她被烧得面目全非，不是吗？

sentences.zh: 他们操作得非常不专业，所以基本上把她烧伤了。

sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.zh: 另一种方法是脑白质切除术。

sentences.zh: 我想这大概是六七年前爆出的故事。

sentences.zh: 我记得我们谈论过，肯尼迪家族也发生过这种事，对吧？

sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.zh: 肯尼迪的一位姐妹就做过脑白质切除术。

sentences.zh: 没错，就是他妹妹，是的。

sentences.zh: 但这在当时是一种标准的医疗程序，旨在缓解脑部压力。

sentences.zh: 是啊，我不知道脑白质切除术的事，汤姆。

sentences.zh: 我没听说过那个故事。

sentences.zh: 嗯，这还有争议。

sentences.zh: 也是。

sentences.zh: 有些人认为这事没发生过。
